title: Why You Need to Change Your Air Filter
desc: Is it time to change your air filter? If so, contact Rosenberg Indoor Comfort to schedule an air conditioning maintenance appointment.

blocks.text: Changing an air filter is one of the simplest maintenance tasks that you can complete. However, it is also one of the most important. Leaving a dirty air filter in place can cause significant damage to your system. Estimates vary on how frequently you ought to do this, and it does depend somewhat on the quality of the filters you use. Ideally, you would change an air conditioner’s air filter every 30 days. Even if you have a relatively dust-free environment and a good filter in place, you should still change it at least every 90 days.
How Do You Know That an Air Filter Is Dirty?

Generally speaking, the filter will get darker as it collects dust, pollen and other material from the air. If you can’t see any light passing through the filter itself, it is a good idea to make a change. Check the air conditioner’s air filter once every week or two to make sure that it is in passable condition. What Happens If You Don’t Change a Dirty Filter?

There are various reasons why you would want to change out your air conditioning filter on a regular basis. First, it will be easier to breathe inside your home because annoying or harmful particles will be trapped by a filter that is clean. This is especially important if members of your household suffer from allergies or respiratory conditions. In addition, the air conditioner itself is less likely to suffer damage because dust and other particles won’t be able to clog motors or coat electrical connections.

An air filter typically costs a few dollars to purchase and a few seconds to put in. However, if you don’t change that filter on a regular basis, you could potentially burn out a motor or impair your equipment in other ways. Even if your unit isn’t rendered inoperable, poor performance will require excess energy and cost more money.
